headline: US futures edge higher — Nasdaq-100 +0.6% as chips rebound — while AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile drop ~7% on SpaceX's spectrum deal and Humana jumps 17% on Medicare star ratings.
notes: Scheduled run at ~7:48 a.m. CT, before the 8:30 a.m. CT open: PRE-MARKET. All movers use live pre-market data dated Oct 9 (StockAnalysis and Yahoo via the Mac browser).

Gap % = pre-market price vs Thursday's close (StockAnalysis). Quality movers screened from Yahoo's US list ≥$5 and ≥$2B with an Oct 9 pre-market quote (1,126 names), then confirmed on StockAnalysis. SBAC (+8.0%, 3.9K shares) and TPC (+5.7%, 264 shares) left out of the movers table as too thinly traded; NRIX, AVNT, PS, SMFG likewise on the losing side.

Relative volume = pre-market volume / 3-month average full-day volume (Yahoo), so values are naturally small before the open.
PCG shows 15.8M pre-market shares on StockAnalysis with the price flat (+0.1%) and no news found — likely a block print; not verified on a second source.

Gap watchlist: telecoms (T, VZ, TMUS) and tower REITs moved on SpaceX's deal, not company-specific news, so they are listed under excluded. LITE/AAOI/COHR excluded: catalyst is Lumentum CEO commentary, not a listed catalyst type. KTOS (+2.9%) and DAL (−2.5%) fell short of the 3% gap.
WTI change differs by source: Yahoo CL=F −0.1% vs Thursday's settle; TheStreet/Yahoo blog cite −0.6% to −0.9% (~$90.7–90.9).
No Fed speakers found on today's schedule in the sources checked. CNBC movers page blocked (Access Denied); Benzinga, TheStreet, TradingKey and the Yahoo live blog used instead.

Under-$5 lists are StockAnalysis top-20 pre-market gainers/losers (~7:57 a.m. CT) filtered to ≥100K shares and <$5 (only 8 gainers qualified); market cap = Yahoo shares outstanding × pre-market price; float not available. VEEA (+53%, $5.94, ~$12M cap) fits neither table. ZBAO (−8%, 170M shares) announced a 1-for-50 reverse split.

Leveraged ETF volume is pre-market volume as a share of a 3-month average day (30-day average not available). NYSE FANG+ has no pre-market quote (underlying_pct null). Proxies: NQ for Nasdaq-100, ES for S&P 500, RTY for Russell 2000, SOXX for semis, XBI for biotech (thin).
Republished at ~4:40 p.m. CT: GitHub's Pages build for the 8:02 a.m. push failed and its re-run got stuck, so the same data was pushed again to start a fresh build.
drivers: Futures are modestly higher, led by the Nasdaq-100 (+0.6%), as chip stocks rebound after Thursday's tech selloff (Nasdaq-100 −1.4%) on an FT report that OpenAI's annualized revenue is near $50 billion; Bloomberg later reported OpenAI expects $70 billion or more by year-end, and NVDA, AMD, AVGO and INTC are up 1–2% pre-market. Oil is easing after Thursday's 4–5% jump: Trump said the US won't attack Iran before the Nov. 3 midterms, Iran is reviewing a US response on reopening the Strait of Hormuz, and Brent is near $103.5; gold is up about 1% to $4,200 and the 10-year yield is near 5.25%. The biggest story is SpaceX agreeing to buy nationwide 800MHz spectrum from Grain Management (about $8 billion) for a Starlink Mobile push, which is knocking AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile down ~7% and lifting tower REITs 6–8%. CMS's 2027 Medicare Advantage star ratings are moving insurers: Humana +17% (flagship contract back to 4 stars, Baird upgrade), Clover +11%, Alignment −19% and CVS −2%. Delta missed Q3 estimates and cut its 2026 EPS outlook on fuel costs, and Apple is −2.6% on a Nikkei report of iPhone 18 Pro order cuts; Canada's September jobs report showed −68K vs +6K expected.
